status: Sourced from official pages where found. Not reviewed by an accountant. Verify before customer launch.

tax_year_basis.uk_self_employed: Forms and notes for 2025-26 (6 Apr 2025 to 5 Apr 2026), the latest published. 2026-27 forms not found at time of research.
tax_year_basis.uk_ltd: Company accounting period, owner-set. No box numbers used.
tax_year_basis.us_schedule_c: Schedule C (Form 1040) 2025 PDF from irs.gov. 2026 draft exists; line numbers may change.
tax_year_basis.hk_profits_tax: Inland Revenue Ordinance s16 and s17. Year of assessment 1 Apr to 31 Mar.

uk_self_employed.label: Cost of goods bought for resale or goods used
uk_self_employed.note: Stock and materials. Traditional-accounting users also adjust opening and closing stock. Goods bought for private use are disallowable (SA103F box 32).

uk_self_employed.label: Construction subcontractor payments
uk_self_employed.note: Payments to subcontractors for construction work. CIS registration may apply.

uk_self_employed.label: Car, van and travel expenses
uk_self_employed.note: Business share only. Home-to-work travel, non-business motoring, fines and other meals are disallowable. Hotel and meals on overnight business trips belong here. Simplified vehicle flat rates are an alternative to actual costs; you cannot use both for the same vehicle.

uk_self_employed.label: Wages, salaries and other staff costs
uk_self_employed.note: Employees and agency or subcontract labour. Your own salary, drawings and NICs are not allowable.

uk_self_employed.label: Rent, rates, power, insurance (incl. business share of home costs)
uk_self_employed.note: Business premises rent, business rates, light, heat, power, property insurance. For a home office: business proportion of household costs, or the simplified flat rate (GBP 10, 18 or 26 per month for 25-50, 51-100 or 101+ hours; minimum 25 hours a month). Flat rate excludes phone and internet.

uk_self_employed.label: Repairs and maintenance of property and equipment
uk_self_employed.note: Repairs, not improvements. Repairs or improvements to non-business parts go in disallowable box 37.

uk_self_employed.label: Phone, stationery and other office costs
uk_self_employed.note: Business share of mixed-use phone and internet. Non-business part goes in disallowable box 38. Small office equipment and software under 2 years old sits here (full form).

uk_self_employed.label: Advertising and marketing
uk_self_employed.note: Newspaper and directory ads, mailshots, free samples, website costs. Client entertaining is NOT in this category (see the next row).

uk_self_employed.label: Entertaining clients, suppliers or customers; hospitality at events
uk_self_employed.tax_box_ref: Not allowable. SA103F box 39 (disallowable); SA103S box 19 says client entertaining is not allowable
uk_self_employed.note: Not allowable. Declare it only as disallowable, or leave it out. Staff entertaining is a separate question (see uk_ltd preset).

uk_self_employed.label: Accountancy, legal and other professional fees
uk_self_employed.note: Fees for running the business. Preparing your Self Assessment return is excluded. Legal costs of buying property or settling tax disputes are disallowable (box 43).

uk_self_employed.label: Bank, credit card and business loan interest and charges
uk_self_employed.note: Bank and card charges, interest on business loans. Capital repayments are not allowable. Non-business part goes in boxes 40-41.

uk_self_employed.label: Trade journals, subscriptions and other running costs
uk_self_employed.note: Trade and professional journals and subscriptions. Payments to clubs, charities, political parties and ordinary clothing are disallowable (box 45).

uk_self_employed.label: Equipment, vehicles and other capital purchases
uk_self_employed.tax_box_ref: Cash basis: payments allowable unless specifically disallowed (SA103S notes). Traditional accounting: not an expense; use capital allowances (SA103S boxes 23-25.2)
uk_self_employed.note: Depends on accounting basis and asset type. Cars have special rules. Annual Investment Allowance is 100% on qualifying equipment (not cars). Professional review needed.

uk_self_employed.label: Fines and penalties
uk_self_employed.tax_box_ref: Disallowable. SA103F box 20 notes (vehicle fines: box 35)
uk_self_employed.note: Fines are listed as disallowable in the SA103F notes, stated for vehicle fines. Treat all fines as no unless an accountant says otherwise.

uk_self_employed.label: Own salary, drawings, own NICs and own pension
uk_self_employed.tax_box_ref: Not an expense (SA103F box 19 notes: not paid to yourself)
uk_self_employed.note: Money you take out for personal use is not an allowable expense.

uk_ltd.label: Staff salaries, wages, PAYE and employer NICs
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: Corporation tax computation (no SA box). Wholly and exclusively for the trade
uk_ltd.note: Run through payroll. Director pay taken as remuneration through payroll is an allowable company expense.

uk_ltd.label: Director's personal expenses paid by the company
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: Not deductible unless part of remuneration. Report on P11D
uk_ltd.note: Personal items are a taxable benefit, reported on P11D. Mixed bills (phone, internet) that cannot be split are not allowable.

uk_ltd.label: Client and customer entertaining
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: Disallowed by statute: CTA 2009 entertainment rule (HMRC BIM45005)
uk_ltd.note: Disallowed even when wholly and exclusively for business. HMRC's own example of a specifically disallowed expense.

uk_ltd.label: Staff entertaining and staff events
uk_ltd.note: Allowable if wholly for business and not merely incidental to customer entertaining. Staff Christmas party and employee-only events are not disallowed.

uk_ltd.label: Business travel and subsistence
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: Corporation tax computation. Wholly and exclusively for the trade
uk_ltd.note: Travel for business purposes. Ordinary commuting is not business travel; confirm the detail with an accountant.

uk_ltd.label: Company car running costs and mileage
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: P11D benefit in kind and Class 1A NIC for private use
uk_ltd.note: Business use is deductible; private use is a benefit, reported on P11D. Car-cost and benefit rules are complex. Professional review needed.

uk_ltd.label: Office rent, rates and utilities
uk_ltd.note: Business premises. Home-office costs charged to the company are a benefit question; ask an accountant.

uk_ltd.label: Phone and internet
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: Corporation tax computation. Only the business part
uk_ltd.note: Only if the business use can be separated. If it cannot be split, the whole bill is not allowable (P11D guidance).

uk_ltd.label: Accountancy, legal and consultancy fees
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: Corporation tax computation. Wholly and exclusively for the trade
uk_ltd.note: Revenue fees for running the company. Legal costs of acquiring assets or share capital are capital, not revenue. Confirm with an accountant.

uk_ltd.label: Bank charges and loan interest
uk_ltd.note: Business charges. Loan interest for companies has specific rules; confirm with an accountant.

uk_ltd.label: Software, hosting and subscriptions
uk_ltd.note: Revenue expense for software used in the business. Capitalisation rules may apply to larger items.

uk_ltd.label: Advertising and marketing
uk_ltd.note: Wholly and exclusively for the trade. Gifts to customers have separate rules; confirm with an accountant.

uk_ltd.label: Equipment and assets (capital)
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: Capital allowances (Annual Investment Allowance 100% on qualifying equipment, not cars)
uk_ltd.note: Capital items are claimed through capital allowances, not as a revenue expense. Professional review needed.

uk_ltd.label: Fines and penalties
uk_ltd.tax_box_ref: Disallowed (general rule; not confirmed on the page cited)
uk_ltd.note: Treat as no until an accountant confirms. The cited page does not list fines specifically.

us_schedule_c.label: Car and truck expenses
us_schedule_c.note: Business-use share only. Standard mileage or actual expenses; choice rules apply. Depreciation is on Form 4562.

us_schedule_c.label: Contract labor
us_schedule_c.note: Payments to independent contractors. Form 1099-NEC reporting may apply.

us_schedule_c.label: Insurance (other than health)
us_schedule_c.note: Business insurance. Health insurance is handled elsewhere on the return.

us_schedule_c.label: Legal and professional services
us_schedule_c.note: Accountants, lawyers, consultants for the business.

us_schedule_c.label: Office expense
us_schedule_c.note: Stationery, small supplies, postage. Personal share is not deductible.

us_schedule_c.label: Rent or lease: other business property (vehicles on line 20a)
us_schedule_c.tax_box_ref: Schedule C Part II line 20a (vehicles) / 20b (other property)
us_schedule_c.note: Business premises or equipment rent. Home-office rent is on line 30 instead.

us_schedule_c.label: Repairs and maintenance
us_schedule_c.note: Repairs, not improvements. Improvements are capitalised.

us_schedule_c.label: Travel
us_schedule_c.note: Airfare, lodging, transport on business trips. Records of time, place and business purpose are required (IRS Pub 463).

us_schedule_c.label: Business meals (50%)
us_schedule_c.note: Business meals at 50%. Receipt needs restaurant name and location, number of people, date and amount. Business purpose written down unless obvious. Entertainment is not deductible.

us_schedule_c.label: Utilities
us_schedule_c.note: Business premises utilities. Home-office share goes on line 30.

us_schedule_c.label: Wages (less employment credits)
us_schedule_c.note: Employee wages only. Owner draws are not wages.

us_schedule_c.label: Other expenses (itemised in Part V, total on line 48, entered on line 27b)
us_schedule_c.tax_box_ref: Schedule C Part II line 27b (from Part V line 48)
us_schedule_c.note: Each Part V line must be an ordinary business expense.

us_schedule_c.label: Business use of home
us_schedule_c.tax_box_ref: Schedule C Part II line 30 (Form 8829, or simplified method worksheet)
us_schedule_c.note: Simplified method: $5 per square foot, up to 300 sq ft (max $1,500). Election is per year and irrevocable once made. No depreciation under simplified method.

us_schedule_c.label: Entertainment (clients, events, recreation)
us_schedule_c.tax_box_ref: Not on any Part II line. Do not report on line 24b (Schedule C instructions)
us_schedule_c.note: Entertainment is generally nondeductible since TCJA. Business meals stay at 50% on line 24b.

hk_profits_tax.label: Office and business premises rent
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s16 (deductible if incurred in producing chargeable profits)
hk_profits_tax.note: Business premises. Home-office share is mixed-use and must be apportioned.

hk_profits_tax.label: Staff salaries and wages
hk_profits_tax.note: Staff employed for the business. Owner's own drawings are private (s17).

hk_profits_tax.label: Utilities (electricity, water)
hk_profits_tax.note: Business premises. Apportion for mixed use.

hk_profits_tax.label: Phone and internet
hk_profits_tax.note: Only the business part. Board of Review D85/02: where a split is possible only the business part is allowed; if the taxpayer cannot prove the business purpose, the whole expense is disallowed.

hk_profits_tax.label: Accounting, audit and legal fees (revenue)
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s16. Capital legal fees excluded by s17(1)(c)
hk_profits_tax.note: Revenue fees only. Capital-related legal costs are not deductible.

hk_profits_tax.label: Client entertaining
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s16 purpose test. No entertaining-specific rule found on the IRD pages reviewed
hk_profits_tax.note: Not verified. The IRD pages reviewed did not state an entertaining rule. Treat as partial, document the business purpose, and ask a Hong Kong practitioner.

hk_profits_tax.label: Business travel
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s16. Home-to-work travel is private (s17)
hk_profits_tax.note: Business trips producing profits. Home-to-work travel is private.

hk_profits_tax.label: Equipment and other capital expenditure
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s17(1)(c) (capital). Depreciation allowances for plant, machinery and computers
hk_profits_tax.note: Capital items are not deducted as expenses; claim the depreciation allowances the IRD page lists.

hk_profits_tax.label: Renovation of business premises
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRD bus_pft: deductible over 5 years in equal instalments
hk_profits_tax.note: Capital spending on renovating business premises may be deducted over 5 years from the year of expense. Specific rules apply.

hk_profits_tax.label: Fines and penalties
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: Not deductible under s16 (Board of Review D99/01)
hk_profits_tax.note: Board of Review decision D99/01 held fines not deductible under s16.

hk_profits_tax.label: Owner's private and domestic costs
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s17 (private or domestic expenses excluded)
hk_profits_tax.note: Private costs and sums not spent to produce profits are excluded.

hk_profits_tax.label: Income tax and profits tax paid
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s17(1)(g): taxes under the IRO are excluded, except salaries tax on employee remuneration
hk_profits_tax.note: Taxes under the IRO are not deductible.

hk_profits_tax.label: Bank charges and business loan interest
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s16 with apportionment. Interest conditions not verified
hk_profits_tax.note: Business loans only. Apportion mixed use. Interest deductibility has its own conditions; not verified here.

hk_profits_tax.label: Overseas VAT or GST charged on purchases
hk_profits_tax.tax_box_ref: IRO s16 if incurred in producing profits (statement from a secondary search summary, not confirmed on the page cited)
hk_profits_tax.note: Hong Kong itself levies no VAT or GST. Foreign VAT or GST is not a profits tax, so it may be deductible; verify with a practitioner.

general.label: Office supplies and stationery
general.note: Ordinary business supplies in every regime reviewed.

general.label: Business travel
general.note: Business purpose only. Commuting treatment differs by country.

general.label: Meals
general.note: US business meals are 50%. UK sole traders cannot claim client meals. Check the country preset.

general.label: Entertainment (clients, events)
general.note: Disallowed in the UK and US. Hong Kong: see hk_client_entertaining, not verified.

general.label: Accountancy, legal and professional fees
general.note: Revenue fees for the business. Your own tax return preparation is excluded in the UK.

general.label: Rent for business premises
general.note: Business premises only. Home-office share is a mixed-use question.

general.label: Staff wages and contractors
general.note: Staff and contractors for the business. Owner's own pay is not an expense.

general.label: Equipment and other capital purchases
general.note: Often claimed as capital allowances rather than an expense. Check the country preset.

general.label: Personal spending (not for the business book)
general.tax_box_ref: none. Personal book only, off by default
general.note: Never an allowable expense. Keep out of the business book.
